newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zairean rebel chief at parade of new fighters.
newsitem.headline: Zairean rebel chief at parade of new fighters.

text.p: East Zairean rebel leader Laurent Kabila presided over a parade of more than 1,000 new rebel troops on Tuesday, signalling the rapid expansion of his force.
The parade held at a Roman Catholic secondary school in Bukavu followed a similar ceremony in the city of Goma last Thursday of some 5,000 newly trained rebels before they were dispatched to fight.
More than 10,000 residents turned out on the pot-holed streets of Bukavu to see the 1,200 new recruits in new U.S. -style combat uniforms, wellington boots and AK-47 assault rifles.

Kabila told the rebels, most of whom were between 15 and 30 years old, he would take the war to the capital Kinshasa and to Gbadolite, which is Mobutu's home village near the border with the Central African Republic.
"We intend to make life impossible for Mobutu. We will deal with him once and for all," Kabila told chanting residents.
Kabila said up to 15,000 new rebels were trained in Bukavu and urged parents to encourage their sons to join the rebels.
He said his forces smashed a government counter-offensive and were advancing on a huge airfield and army base at Kindu.
"We have defeated Mobutu's counter-offensive once and for all. We are advancing on many fronts and what now remains is for us to uproot Mobutu from power," Kabila added.
Rebel officials with Kabila told Reuters that rebel forces were closing in on Kindu, a mining town, which also has a large French-built airport and is 340 km (200 miles) west of Bukavu.
They said rebels had also surrounded Isiro town near the Sudan-Uganda border and the tin and gold mining town of Punia.
They said that other forces were edging towards the southern lake port of Moba and the town of Kabambare on the way to Kindu.
Kabila said on Sunday his forces were 25 km (15 miles) from Moba, which the government army was reinforcing by rail and air from the military base at Kamina.
Kindu and Kisangani are the only two airports held by government forces in eastern Zaire. The other airports at Bunia, Goma, Bukavu, Uvira, Kamanyola and Kalemie are held by rebels.
Kabila's Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire (ADFL) says it has seized a border strip about 1,400 km (875 miles) long since the revolt began in October.

U.N. officials said a U.N. team flying over eastern Zaire spotted a group of between 15,000 and 20,000 refugees on Sunday at Kalima west of Shabunda, which Kinshasa said its forces recaptured last week but rebels say is still in their hands.
They said church groups in Kalima, 145 km (90 miles) west of Kindu, were prepared to distribute what medicine and food was brought in but it was unknown how long the refugees would stay.
Zaire on Monday welcomed a proposal by a European Union special envoy for a regional meeting before any international conference on the conflict-ridden Great Lakes region.
Aldo Ajello arrived in Zaire on Saturday and met President Mobutu Sese Seko in Gbadolite on Sunday and the foreign minister on Monday in Kinshasa.
The foreign ministry said the intended meeting would gather not only the heads of states who took part in last year's Nairobi summit but also those from other African countries and donors as well.
